summary.text: Upturned German battleship scuttled in 1919 in Scapa Flow, the shallowest of the big three. Its hull top is near 12-14 m and several main guns can be seen, making it the most approachable battleship dive.

summary.text: Deepest of the three scuttled German battleships at Scapa Flow, lying upside down on its port side, with the hull rising to roughly 23 m above a seabed near 45 m. A demanding, deeper dive than its sisters.

summary.text: German light cruiser scuttled in 1919 and never raised, resting on her starboard side in Scapa Flow. Her top is about 22 m and the seabed 36 m, and she is a straightforward wreck for competent sport divers.

summary.text: Bayern was raised in the 1930s but her four main-gun turrets fell off and still lie upside down on the mud of Scapa Flow. They sit in two pairs and a rope now links them, so all four can be seen in one dive.

summary.text: Remains of the 1993 tanker Braer off Garths Ness, smashed flat in shallow water under 10 m. Little is recognisable and the site is very exposed to the wind.

summary.text: Remains of a 1588 Spanish Armada supply ship scattered in rocky gullies at Stroms Hellier on Fair Isle. Divers have found the large anchor among boulders; little hull structure survives.
